questions.text: What is preserved by a PostgreSQL logical backup?

answers.text: A logical representation of objects and data that can later be recreated
An exact byte-for-byte copy of all PGDATA
Only WAL segments
Only server configuration files

questions.explanation: Logical backup works at the level of objects, their definitions, and data, unlike physical copying of cluster files.

questions.text: Which tasks can COPY perform? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: Export table contents
Export a query result
Load rows into an existing table
Create a physical copy of the entire cluster

questions.explanation: COPY exchanges table data with files or streams; it does not create a physical copy of PGDATA.

source.locator: Backup and restore of individual data

questions.text: Who must be able to access the file when the server-side SQL COPY command is used?

answers.text: The operating-system user running the PostgreSQL server
Only the user who started psql
Any database user regardless of file-system permissions
Only the SQL owner of the source table

questions.explanation: SQL COPY is executed by the server, so the file must be accessible to the PostgreSQL server process.

questions.text: Which differences between SQL COPY and psql \copy are correct? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: SQL COPY is the server-side variant
\copy performs the file operation on the psql client side
For \copy, the file must be accessible to the user who started psql
\copy always creates a complete database dump

questions.explanation: The main difference is which side opens the file: the server for COPY or the client for \copy.

questions.text: Which utility is intended for creating a complete logical backup of a single database?

answers.text: pg_dump
pg_basebackup
pg_receivewal
pg_ctl

questions.explanation: The lesson presents pg_dump as the primary tool for logical backup of one database.

questions.text: Which outputs can pg_dump produce? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: An SQL script
An archive in a special format with a table of contents
A dump of a limited set of objects
A byte-for-byte copy of the PGDATA directory

questions.explanation: The material shows SQL output and special archive formats, as well as the ability to select dumped tables, schemas, DDL, or data.

questions.text: How do you restore a pg_dump backup represented as a plain SQL script?

answers.text: Execute the script with psql
Pass it to pg_basebackup
Copy it into pg_wal
Pass it to pg_receivewal

questions.explanation: An SQL dump already consists of SQL commands, so it is restored by executing those commands with a PostgreSQL client.

questions.text: Which capabilities does pg_restore provide? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: Restore pg_dump archives in special formats
Restrict the set of objects at restore time
Support parallel restore for suitable formats
Restore only completed WAL segments

questions.explanation: The advantage of an archive format is its table of contents, which allows object selection during restore and parallel operation.

questions.text: Which template should be used to create a new database before restoring a complete dump?

answers.text: template0
template1
postgres
pg_global

questions.explanation: The notes explicitly say to create the target database from template0 before restoration.

questions.text: What may need to be prepared before restoring a dump of a single database? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: Required roles
Required tablespaces
The target database
All source WAL segments from the database lifetime

questions.explanation: A dump of one database is not a complete copy of all cluster-wide global objects, so dependencies such as roles and tablespaces must already exist.

questions.text: Which utility is intended for a logical backup of an entire cluster, including global objects?

answers.text: pg_dumpall
pg_restore
pg_receivewal
COPY

questions.explanation: pg_dumpall dumps the cluster databases in sequence and stores information that applies to the cluster as a whole.

questions.text: Which statements about pg_dumpall are correct? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: It saves the cluster databases
It saves global objects, including roles and tablespaces
Its output is an SQL script
Its output is always an archive for pg_restore

questions.explanation: Unlike pg_dump with its archive formats, pg_dumpall produces an SQL script for later execution.

questions.text: Why is pg_dumpall recommended to be run as a superuser?

answers.text: The utility needs access to all objects in all cluster databases
Otherwise it cannot read WAL
Otherwise PostgreSQL cannot be started
Because pg_dumpall always runs initdb

questions.explanation: pg_dumpall connects to the cluster databases and needs sufficient privileges to read all objects being saved.

source.locator: Access to all databases and objects

questions.text: Which approaches allow pg_dump and pg_dumpall to be combined? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: Dump global objects with pg_dumpall
Dump individual databases with pg_dump
Use this approach instead of a full pg_dumpall when more convenient
Use pg_dump for streaming WAL reception

questions.explanation: The notes explicitly mention saving global objects separately while backing up individual databases with pg_dump.

questions.text: How is the output of a regular full pg_dumpall restored?

answers.text: As an SQL script through psql
Only through pg_restore
Through pg_basebackup
Through restore_command

questions.explanation: pg_dumpall produces an SQL script, so restoration is performed by executing that script.

questions.text: An administrator needs to restore only some objects from an existing archive dump. Which properties of the chosen approach are correct? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: The dump must use a suitable special pg_dump format
pg_restore is used for restoration
The set of restored objects can be restricted at restore time
A WAL archive is mandatory

questions.explanation: An archive format with a table of contents allows pg_restore to select the required objects after the backup has already been created.

questions.text: Which statements about PostgreSQL logical backup are correct? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: A copy can contain individual objects or a single database
A logical copy can be moved between compatible PostgreSQL major versions
The logical approach allows migration between different hardware architectures
It allows recovery to any point in time after the dump was created without WAL

questions.explanation: A logical copy is flexible and portable, but by itself it captures the state at dump time and is not a PITR mechanism.

source.locator: Advantages and limitations of logical backup

questions.text: Which statements about pg_dump are correct? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: The dump represents a consistent snapshot of the database as of the start of pg_dump
Normal database operations can continue while the dump is running
pg_dump is a client application and can run from a remote machine if it has access
For consistency, pg_dump must stop the server for the entire dump

questions.explanation: pg_dump obtains a consistent snapshot without stopping normal server activity and connects like a regular PostgreSQL client.
